sites.name: Ta Dung Lake
sites.event: Known as the 'Ha Long Bay of the Central Highlands', located in Ta Dung National Park with more than 36 large and small islands.

sites.name: Chu Bluk Volcanic Cave (Dray Sap)
sites.event: The longest volcanic cave system in Southeast Asia, an important highlight of the UNESCO Dak Nong Global Geopark.

sites.name: Dak Mil Prison Historical Relic
sites.event: The prison was built by the French colonialists in 1940 to detain and exile revolutionary soldiers.

sites.name: Lieng Nung Waterfall
sites.event: A majestic waterfall with a unique hexagonal cliff geological structure, deeply imbued with the legends of the M'nong people.

sites.name: B4 Resistance Base - Interprovincial IV
sites.event: An important revolutionary base of the resistance forces of Zone 6 and Zone 10 during the anti-American resistance war (located in the Nam Nung Nature Reserve).

sites.name: Dray Sap Waterfall
sites.event: One of the most majestic waterfalls in the Central Highlands, its name means 'Smoke Waterfall' due to the year-round white water spray.

sites.name: Hill 722 - Dak Sak Historical Relic
sites.event: A special forces camp of the US-puppet regime, where many fierce battles took place during the Vietnam War.

sites.name: Truc Lam Dao Nguyen Zen Monastery
sites.event: A Buddhist architectural work hidden amidst the vast pine forests of the Nam Nung Nature Reserve.

sites.name: N'Trang Long Hero Monument
sites.event: A monument commemorating the leader of the anti-French colonial uprising of the ethnic groups in the Central Highlands.

sites.name: Gia Long Waterfall (Dray Sap Thuong)
sites.event: Associated with the legend that King Gia Long once came here to rest and admire the beautiful scenery.
